issues.body:
`_alert_route` is called in production with three arguments (metrics-alert.py:362 and :395), so the live path is the default `check = confirmed_private if confirmed_private is not None else _repo_confirmed_private`. Nothing pins that binding:

- Every unit row supplies an explicit lambda (:610 `lambda r,t: True`, :613 `lambda r,t: False`, the same-repo row), so `confirmed_private is not None` and the default is never taken.
- Every row that does use the default (:621 empty token, :623 None token, no-repo rows) short-circuits on `if alert_repo and alert_token` before `check` is ever consulted.
- The one end-to-end harness that reaches the branch, `run_main` (:798), hardcodes `responses[("api", "repos/org/private")] = _Result(0, json.dumps({"private": True}))` at :802, and the wiring assertion at :978-982 only checks the HAPPY path (`private route -> -R org/private under ALERT_TOKEN`).

So the mutant `else (lambda r, t: True)` — which is byte-for-byte the pre-PR behaviour the PR exists to remove — passes the entire suite. The same hole is present in all six changed files: ci-latency-alert.py and triage-stock-alert.py have no main() flow test reaching the branch at all; dispatch-stall-alert.py's `_test_gh_flows` explicitly pops ALERT_REPO/ALERT_TOKEN before calling main(); groom-mint-alert.py:1358 and park-stock-alert.py:712 stub the probe to `private: True` only.

This is the exact case the repo already solved. usage-alert.py:996-1017 runs the SAME configuration twice, flipping only the stubbed visibility, and its comment at :999-1000 says: 'Reverting _alert_route to trust configuration alone turns (4) RED — that is the exact fail-open the finding names.' plan-alert.py:558 and groom-alert.py:358 carry the same `visibility='{"private": false}'` end-to-end row.
issues.fix_hint: In each of the six files, add a NEGATIVE end-to-end row that drives the alert-emitting path with ALERT_REPO and ALERT_TOKEN both non-empty and the stubbed `gh api repos/{ALERT_REPO}` answering something other than `{"private": true}` (e.g. `{"private": false}` or junk), asserting the alert lands on the REGISTRY repo under the ambient token. Model it on usage-alert.py:1006-1017 (loop over `private_ok` True/False with `want_repo` org/private vs org/registry) or plan-alert.py:558. For metrics-alert.py, extend `run_main` with a `visibility=` parameter feeding `responses[("api", "repos/org/private")]` and add the fail-closed counterpart beside the :978-982 wiring row. For ci-latency-alert.py, dispatch-stall-alert.py and triage-stock-alert.py — which have no harness reaching the branch — either add one or, at minimum, assert the default binding directly, e.g. monkeypatch `_repo_confirmed_private` to a recording stub and assert `_alert_route(repo, token, registry)` consulted it with `(repo, token)`.
issues.title: Vacuous on the actual fix: no test distinguishes the real visibility probe from an unconditional `True` — reverting the fail-open keeps all six self-tests green

issues.body:
`_private_probe_rows` (:1153-1170) rebinds the module global `_gh` and then asserts only that `_repo_confirmed_private` passed `["api", "repos/org/private"]` with `{"capture": True, "token": "route-token"}` as a keyword to `_gh` (:1530-1531). That seam is one call short of the property that matters: `_gh` (:890-901) is what actually copies `token` into `env["GH_TOKEN"]`, and it is stubbed out. A regression in which `_gh` stops honouring `token=` — sending the visibility probe under the ambient registry credential instead of ALERT_TOKEN — is invisible to this test in all six files.

The already-hardened siblings deliberately stub one level lower: plan-alert.py:585-586 and groom-alert.py:385-386 monkeypatch `subprocess.run` and assert the full realised shape `(["gh", "api", "repos/org/private"], "route-tok")`, pinning the argv AND the token as it actually lands in the environment.

This matters beyond style: a probe issued under the wrong credential can answer `private: false` for a repo the ALERT token can see (or 404 -> rc!=0), silently degrading every deployment to the registry fallback; or, on a token with broader scope, confirm privacy the alert token itself cannot rely on.
issues.fix_hint: Stub `subprocess.run` rather than the `_gh` global in `_private_probe_rows`, and assert the realised command and credential together, e.g. capture `(list(cmd), (env or {}).get("GH_TOKEN"))` and pin it to `(["gh", "api", "repos/org/private"], "route-token")`, matching plan-alert.py:585-586 / groom-alert.py:385-386. Apply to all six copies.
issues.title: `_private_probe_rows` stubs the module-global `_gh`, so it never proves the route token reaches GH_TOKEN on the real `gh` invocation

issues.body:
The new docstring (:167-172) asserts the router is 'identical semantics and signature to the other alert routers'. After this PR 11 of 13 routers carry the `confirmed_private` form, but `scripts/ratelimit-alert.py:363` and `scripts/ledger-identity-watch.py:245` still have the presence-only three-argument `_alert_route(alert_repo, alert_token, registry_repo)` and will keep routing alerts to an unverified, possibly public ALERT_REPO. The same claim is made in ci-latency-alert.py:1139, groom-mint-alert.py:170 and metrics-alert.py:126.

In this repo the router prose is load-bearing rather than decorative — park-stock-alert.py and triage-stock-alert.py lock their docstrings under `canonical_route_doc` equality guards precisely so the stated contract cannot drift from the code. A blanket 'identical to the other routers' claim that is false for two of them is the kind of drift those guards exist to prevent, and it makes the estate look uniformly hardened when two lanes are not.
issues.fix_hint: Either convert scripts/ratelimit-alert.py and scripts/ledger-identity-watch.py in this PR (preferred — it makes the claim true and finishes the migration), or soften the wording to name the verified set rather than asserting estate-wide identity, and file a tracking issue for the two stragglers.
issues.title: Docstring claims semantics 'identical to the other alert routers' while two routers remain presence-only

issues.body:
`ambient()` (:730-736) still documents itself as returning the GH_TOKEN seen on 'the ONE call `main()` makes with `token=None`'. That is no longer true: main() now issues at least two `gh api` calls — the PR census (`/pulls?...`, ambient token) and the new visibility probe (`repos/{ALERT_REPO}`, under ALERT_TOKEN). The code was correctly updated to disambiguate by filtering on `"/pulls?" in cmd[2]` (:733-735, and the matching change at :764-765), but the prose beside it still describes the old single-call world.

Left as is, the comment invites a future reader to 'simplify' the filter back to `routed("api")`, which would now non-deterministically pick up the visibility probe and silently assert against the wrong credential — the precise failure the surrounding #1773 comment warns about.
issues.fix_hint: Reword the `ambient()` docstring to state that main() now makes two `api` calls — the PR census under the ambient token and the visibility probe under ALERT_TOKEN — and that this helper deliberately selects the census leg by its `/pulls?` path.
issues.title: `ambient()` docstring is now stale — main() no longer makes exactly one `api` call

issues.body:
`_private_probe_rows` (:418-431) packs multiple statements per line with semicolons (`_gh = response(rc, body); values.append(...)`, `calls.append((args, kwargs)); return ...`) and a same-line `finally: _gh = original`, and carries no docstring. The copy the same PR adds to ci-latency-alert.py:1153-1170 is the expanded, documented form ('Exercise every fail-closed result of this module's live repository probe.').

Since these bodies are meant to be recognisably identical across the estate — that mutual identity is what the docstring guards and the cross-script contract tests trade on — the divergence makes a future diff-of-copies read as a real difference. The same compressed form appears in dispatch-stall-alert.py, groom-mint-alert.py, metrics-alert.py and park-stock-alert.py. (No ruff config or lint job is present in the repo, so this is not a CI failure — E701/E702 would flag it under ruff defaults if one is ever added.)
issues.fix_hint: Normalise all five compressed copies to the expanded, docstringed form already used in ci-latency-alert.py:1153-1170 so the six helpers are textually identical.
issues.title: Compressed one-liner style in `_private_probe_rows` diverges from the readable copy in the same PR

verdict.summary:
The change is directionally right and mostly well built: it ports the already-hardened usage-alert.py/plan-alert.py/groom-alert.py visibility-probe pattern to six more routers, correctly fails closed on rc!=0 / unparseable / non-boolean `private`, correctly rejects a same-repo ALERT_REPO case-insensitively BEFORE spending a lookup, and drops the old prose claim that token presence proves ALERT_TOKEN 'can write there' (which was itself a false capability claim). The metrics-alert.py authority-surface widening is properly compensated: adding `api` to the noun vocabulary is fenced by a new api_shapes row pinning exactly one call site, exactly two argv elements, an f-string literal-prefixed `repos/`, and no mutation flag, so `-X POST` cannot be smuggled in. The `[OPUS-5]` -> `[SPARQ agent]` header renames are correct per model-agnostic identity. The park/triage docstring-equality guards and their `anchor` were updated consistently and the anchor still occurs exactly once.

Blocking defect: the security property being added is not pinned by any test in any of the six files. `_alert_route`'s default binding (`else _repo_confirmed_private`) is the production path at every call site (ci-latency:3063, dispatch:591, groom-mint:584, triage:475, park:282), but every unit row passes an explicit `lambda r, t: True/False`, and every fail-closed row short-circuits on an empty repo/token before the check is consulted. The only end-to-end harnesses that reach the branch (metrics `run_main`, groom-mint/park `fake_run`) stub the probe to `private: true` only. Consequently, replacing `else _repo_confirmed_private` with `else (lambda r, t: True)` -- i.e. reverting to exactly the pre-PR fail-open this PR exists to fix -- leaves all six self-tests GREEN. The repo's own precedent rejects this: usage-alert.py:996-1017 and plan-alert.py:558 / groom-alert.py:358 each pin a NEGATIVE end-to-end run with `"private": false`, and usage-alert.py:999 states the requirement outr… [truncated 139 chars]
